These fixtures pin Joern v4.0.555's additional TYPE registration during
declaration initialization. An uninitialized `unsigned char value;` registers
`unsigned char`; `unsigned char value = 0;` additionally registers `unsigned`.
A later assignment does not take the initializer path. An array's implicit
allocation does not take it either.

The 47 isolated projects under `cases/` cover local and global objects,
pointers, arrays, mixed declarators, loop declarations, subsequent assignments,
qualifiers and integer/floating widths. They also separate an initialized
function pointer from its uninitialized ordinary neighbor: only the ordinary
object's own initializer triggers the additional primitive registration. Two
typedef cases preserve their previous complete graphs. Each project
has a fresh type pool, so another declaration cannot mask a spurious TYPE.

All 5,708 selected records agree with the live oracle. The accepted baseline
is `ad1cee71d` plus the independent method-address definition repair
`fd374db1d`, reproduced here by dependency commit `44afeacfd`. Complete graph
agreement improves from 22 to 47 projects, with no formerly exact graph lost.
These counts describe these inputs and this projection, not a C completion
percentage. [measurement.json](measurement.json) binds the source, reference,
raw oracle outputs and both frozen binary hashes for all 62 investigation
probes, including the fifteen remaining diagnostics.

Every `expected.txt` contains the entire selected AST, NODES, EDGES and FLOWS
output for that project. Only the `AST|` transport prefix is removed. The
production regressions compare all records and separately verify retained
LOCAL types, EVAL_TYPE edges, source locations and assignment calls:

```sh
cd cpg-rs
cargo test --locked -p joern-parity --test declaration_registration
```

To regenerate the 47 conformant references, run from the repository root
with `JOERN` pointing to the pinned executable and `JAVA_HOME` to JDK 21:

```sh
fixture="$PWD/cpg-rs/joern-parity/tests/fixtures"
scratch=$(mktemp -d)
(cd "$scratch" && "$JOERN" \
  --script "$fixture/primitive-roles/isolated-oracle.sc" \
  --param inputPath="$fixture/declaration-registration/cases" \
  > live.stdout 2> live.stderr)
```

The driver uses the unchanged projection from `joern-parity/oracle.sc` and
separates fresh imports with `CASE|directory`. Retain all selected records for
each case when comparing or regenerating a reference.

`diagnostics/` retains fifteen additional inputs, their complete live references,
and complete baseline/candidate diffs. They are not included in the passing
fixture count: two initializer-list arrays, one local string-initialized
array, an invalid scalar-initialized array, five function pointers with
`(void)` parameter lists, and six tagged-type cases. The array lowering and
function-pointer signature differences predate this repair. The registration change removes the extra
prefix type in three mixed callback diagnostics; it does not change their
remaining signature mismatch. The six tagged-type outputs are byte-identical
to the accepted baseline, preserving their independent base registration and
their preexisting scaffold/type differences. A production test separately
asserts the retained struct and enum TYPE records. The union base spelling
remains among the preserved differences. These inputs can be regenerated by passing
`diagnostics` instead of `cases` to the same driver.

The primitive initializer rule follows the extra `registerType` call in pinned
Joern's
[`astForInitializer`](https://github.com/joernio/joern/blob/v4.0.555/joern-cli/frontends/c2cpg/src/main/scala/io/joern/c2cpg/astcreation/AstForTypesCreator.scala#L128-L132).
Nonprimitive declarations keep their previous registration behavior: tagged
types can register a base type independently of initialization. This repair
does not change primitive spellings, casts, typedef expansion,
aggregate lowering or literal types, and does not establish full C parity.
